frame: robot frame, mm: X forward, Y left, Z up, origin at the Go2's body centre

sustained_stowed.note: the folded arm's weight, always on the mount

working_full_reach.note: robot lying (the arm moves only stopped and down); arm stretched out at its measured 0.67 m reach with the rated 1.5 kg at the tip, forward/back (about Y) or to the side (about X); x1.5 for the arm's own accelerations (est.)

walking_stowed.note: each step: vertical 0 to 2 g on the stowed arm (range 2 g), 0.5 g sideways and fore-aft (est., trot); 1e7 cycles design life ([Xtj])

lying_and_standing.note: lying down and standing up with the arm stowed: 1.5 g and a 20 deg pitch (est.)

fall_onto_back.note: the robot rolls onto its back: the stowed arm's mass at 8 g, pushing the arm toward the body (est.: ~0.3 m drop onto a rug or hard floor with ~4 mm of give at the arm); the arm may scuff, the mount must not let go of it

pieces: no piece needs splitting: each fits the X1's 256 mm cube with margin (see report), so no printed joints inside a part; the joints above are the assembly's

layers.adapter: printed upside down, deck on the bed: layers are XY planes, so bending along X (the arm's moment) and the twist both run in the layers; the bolt clamp and the deck's bearing press across them
layers.module: printed top-down: the same; the arm base's bolts pull across the layers (6 mm of top skin)
layers.bin: printed upright: walls along Z; a knock bends the walls across the layers (PETG or PC, low stress)

status: estimates, 4 Oct 2026; the printed parts' measured stiffness replaces them ([lUO])
